user.title: Set up NetOrbit
user.description: Pick the network to map. NetOrbit pings devices on this subnet and reads Home Assistant's ARP table to learn their MAC addresses. Everything you set up is remembered by MAC address, so DHCP changing a device's IP is fine. For the tidiest map, give your router, switches and access points DHCP reservations.

data_description.subnet: In CIDR form, for example 10.0.0.0/24. Up to 1024 hosts.
data_description.gateway: Your router. It becomes the center of the map.
data_description.mode: Automatic tracks everything it finds. Manual only tracks devices you add and lists the rest as new.
data_description.ping_interval: How often tracked devices are pinged.

error.invalid_subnet: That is not a valid IPv4 subnet.
error.subnet_too_large: That subnet is too large. Use /22 or smaller.
error.invalid_ip: That is not a valid IP address.
error.gateway_outside: The router IP has to be inside the subnet.

abort.already_configured: This subnet is already set up.

create_entry.default:
NetOrbit is now finding the devices on your network. **One more step to see the map:** open a dashboard, click the pencil (Edit dashboard), choose **Add card**, search for **NetOrbit**, and save.

For a full-screen map, make a dashboard just for it and set its view type to **Panel (single card)**. If NetOrbit isn't in the card search, refresh your browser.

[Step-by-step guide]({guide_url})

data.auto_hubs: Add hubs automatically when NetOrbit is sure

data_description.discovery_interval: How often the whole subnet is swept for new devices.
data_description.stale_hours: A device that has not answered for this long turns red and fires a netorbit_device_stale event.
data_description.ignore_random_mac: Phones and laptops often use a private address per network. Leave this on to keep them off the map.
data_description.auto_hubs: When off, everything NetOrbit finds is listed under Review suggested hubs instead.
data_description.group_by_type: On networks where nothing reports which access point a device uses, the card groups devices into TVs, computers, smart home and so on.
data_description.check_internet: Each ping round also pings two public DNS servers (1.1.1.1 and 8.8.8.8). The Internet node turns red when neither answers for two rounds while your router still does, and fires netorbit_internet_down and netorbit_internet_up events.
data_description.snmp_enabled: NetOrbit asks each device once an hour whether it is a managed switch, using read-only SNMP, then reads the switch's MAC table to place devices automatically.
data_description.snmp_community: Leave empty to try the factory default. If you changed your switches' read-only community, enter it here.
data_description.prefer_dns_names: Show the name your network gives a device (reverse DNS, or the name it announces over Bonjour) before names from other integrations, and use it for hubs NetOrbit named itself, such as the router. Names you typed are always kept.
data_description.weak_signal_minutes: A device whose radio signal has read below good (−80 dBm, LQI 80) for this many minutes is drawn in a yellow-green between online and seen-recently, and the popup says for how long; the clock only stops once the signal reads clearly good again (−75 dBm, LQI 100), so a device hovering at the threshold counts. 0 never colours it.
data_description.offline_after_rounds: How many ping rounds in a row a flagged hub or device may miss before it counts as offline and fires netorbit_device_offline. 3 rounds at a 60 s ping interval means one dropped Wi-Fi packet never pages you.
data_description.port_counters: Each ping round, read every managed switch's port byte counters (three short SNMP walks per switch) and draw busier links wider. Turn off to keep the MAC tables but skip the counters.

review_new.description: Devices seen on the network that are not tracked yet.

review_hubs.title: Suggested hubs
review_hubs.description: NetOrbit thinks these might be routers, switches, access points or mesh nodes.

paste_list.title: Paste a client list
paste_list.description: Open the client or device list for one access point, mesh node or switch (its web page or phone app), copy everything, and paste it here. NetOrbit picks out the MAC and IP addresses and places those devices under the hub you choose.

add_controller.title: Add a Wi-Fi controller
add_controller.description: A Wi-Fi controller tells NetOrbit which access point each wireless device uses, with its signal, band and channel, and NetOrbit places those devices under their access points. NetOrbit only reads from it.

data_description.kind: The product that manages your access points. Each type is a small plug-in module.

data_description.controller: The controller to change or remove.

data_description.name: How the controller is shown on the map (the device's source line says "from <name>"). Empty uses the host.
data_description.host: Address of the controller's management interface.
data_description.port: Its HTTPS API port (443 unless you changed it).
data_description.verify_ssl: Off for a controller with its factory certificate; turn on once it has a certificate your Home Assistant trusts.
data_description.token: A read-only API token. On an edit, leave empty to keep the saved one.
data_description.password: Its password. On an edit, leave empty to keep the saved one.
data_description.remove: Tick to delete this controller and its credentials from the settings.

error.invalid_ip: That is not a valid IP address.
error.hub_cycle: A hub cannot be connected through itself.
error.pick_or_ip: Pick a device or enter a valid IP address.
error.hub_exists: Another hub already uses that address.
error.no_addresses: No MAC or IP addresses were found in that text.
error.no_matches: None of those addresses match a device on this network.
error.not_loaded: NetOrbit is not running right now. Try again in a minute.
error.bad_fields: Write each extra field on its own line as Label: value. A field may hold up to 500 characters, and a hub or device up to 20 fields.
error.cannot_connect: Could not reach the controller at that address and port, or it answered with an error.
error.invalid_auth: The controller refused the token or password.
error.unknown_kind: This controller was saved by a build with a plug-in that is not installed here. It can only be removed.
